title: Secret of the Parable: Presence of the Master and Acceptance of His Word

questions.question: What two things must happen for the ruler’s goals for the palace to be reached?
questions.answer: The teacher must be there, and the people must listen to him and follow his words.

questions.question: Why is the teacher so important in the palace story?
questions.answer: He explains the meaning and purpose of the palace.

questions.question: What picture is used to show why a teacher is needed?
questions.answer: A hard-to-understand book without a teacher is like paper with no real meaning.

questions.question: What does the passage say the teacher’s being there causes?
questions.answer: It is the reason the palace was built.

questions.question: What does the people’s listening to the teacher cause?
questions.answer: It helps the palace stay as it is and continue.

questions.question: What might the ruler have done if there were no teacher at all?
questions.answer: He would not have built the palace.

questions.question: What happens if people do not pay attention to the teacher’s directions?
questions.answer: The palace will surely be changed into something else.

questions.question: Is the passage teaching that hearing the teacher is enough, or that people should also follow him?
questions.answer: They should also follow him.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: The teacher and the people’s obedience are both necessary for the palace’s purpose.

questions.question: Who is speaking to the listener in this passage?
questions.answer: A friend is speaking to another friend.

questions.question: What does the speaker say the listener has already understood?
questions.answer: That the great ruler built the palace for the goals told earlier.

questions.question: How many main things does the passage say those goals depend on?
questions.answer: Two.

questions.question: What is the first of those two things?
questions.answer: The teacher must exist.

questions.question: What is the second of those two things?
questions.answer: The people must accept what the teacher says and act on it.

questions.question: How does the example of the difficult book help us understand the palace?
questions.answer: It shows that without someone to explain, people cannot understand what they are looking at.

questions.question: What does the passage connect to the start of the palace?
questions.answer: The presence of the teacher.

questions.question: What does the passage connect to the palace continuing on?
questions.answer: The people listening to the teacher.

questions.question: What warning is given at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: If people ignore the teacher, the palace will definitely be changed.

questions.question: What is one needed means named first in the passage?
questions.answer: The teacher.

questions.question: What work does the teacher do for the palace?
questions.answer: He helps people understand it.

questions.question: What would an unclear book be like if no one taught it?
questions.answer: It would seem empty of meaning.

questions.question: What must the people do after hearing the teacher?
questions.answer: They must accept his words and pay attention to them.

questions.question: Which is linked to the palace being made: the people’s listening or the teacher’s existence?
questions.answer: The teacher’s existence.

questions.question: Which is linked to the palace remaining as it should: the teacher’s existence or the people’s listening?
questions.answer: The people’s listening.

questions.question: What can we infer about people who ignore the teacher?
questions.answer: They miss the palace’s purpose and bring about change.

questions.question: What lesson does this give about guidance?
questions.answer: Good guidance matters, and people must respond to it.

questions.question: What does the passage say is certain about the ruler building the palace?
questions.answer: He built it for the goals already mentioned.

questions.question: What word in the passage shows that reaching those goals is tied closely to two things?
questions.answer: It says the goals depend on two things.

questions.question: What is the first thing the goals depend on?
questions.answer: Having the teacher.

questions.question: What simple example is given to explain this first thing?
questions.answer: A book no one can understand needs a teacher or it is useless to readers.

questions.question: What is the second thing the goals depend on?
questions.answer: The people receiving the teacher’s message and following it.

questions.question: If the teacher is present but the people refuse to listen, what will happen in the end?
questions.answer: The palace will be changed.

questions.question: Which matters come first in order: the teacher being there or the people listening?
questions.answer: The teacher being there comes first.

questions.question: What cause-and-effect teaching fills this whole passage?
questions.answer: Right guidance and listening to it lead to the palace’s purpose being fulfilled.

questions.question: What does the speaker call the person who is listening?
questions.answer: Friend.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the ruler’s goals for the palace?
questions.answer: They can only be reached in a certain way.

questions.question: What is one thing needed for those goals to be reached?
questions.answer: The teacher must exist.

questions.question: What is another thing needed?
questions.answer: The people must listen to the teacher and accept his message.

questions.question: Why is the teacher compared to someone who explains a hard book?
questions.answer: Because he makes hidden meaning clear.

questions.question: Without explanation, how would the palace be like that hard book?
questions.answer: People would not understand what it means.

questions.question: What strong claim does the passage make about the palace and the teacher?
questions.answer: Without the teacher, the ruler would not have made the palace.

questions.question: What strong claim does the passage make about people who ignore the teacher?
questions.answer: Their ignoring him leads to the palace being altered.

questions.question: Does the passage treat listening as a small extra thing or as something very important?
questions.answer: It treats it as very important.

questions.question: What is one big lesson a student can learn from this passage?
questions.answer: We need true teaching, and we should listen carefully to it.

questions.question: What has the listener clearly understood by this point in the story?
questions.answer: That the ruler built the palace for special purposes.

questions.question: What does the passage say those purposes rely on?
questions.answer: Two important things.

questions.question: Name the first important thing.
questions.answer: The teacher being there.

questions.question: Name the second important thing.
questions.answer: The people accepting the teacher’s words and obeying them.

questions.question: Why does the passage say all the purposes would be wasted without the teacher?
questions.answer: Because the meaning would stay hidden.

questions.question: What example from reading is used to teach that point?
questions.answer: A confusing book without someone to teach it.

questions.question: According to the passage, what role does the teacher have in relation to the palace itself?
questions.answer: His presence is the reason for its building.

questions.question: According to the passage, what role do the people have in relation to the palace staying in place?
questions.answer: Their listening is the reason it continues.

questions.question: What future result is promised if the people stop listening?
questions.answer: The palace will certainly be changed and transformed.

questions.question: In one sentence, what is the message of the whole passage?
questions.answer: The palace’s purpose needs both a true teacher and people who listen to him.
